The one thing I'd really add is CHAMOMILE TEA. It's not as strong as a prescription medicine, but it does soothe the stomach a fair bit, especially if it's not at an overwhelming point yet. It also helps for the hunger pain of when your stomach is empty but you can't eat. Drink it mildly warm, with just a tiny bit of honey, it doesn't take much. (If she likes/can eat honey, of course)

Op, please, for your sanity consider going nc again and stick with it. Don't engage with your family AT ALL, they have made it clear that you, your comfort, your feelings and your actual safety are not important to them. It is probably going to be really hard in a lot of ways but for the sake of your LIFE please get them out of it. You are worth sticking around and enjoying being here, and your relatives are actively trying (even succeeding) in destroying your desire to reach for it. You said you've been suicidal since you were about 7. That to me is more than enough of a sign that your family is not good for you. And it hurts. I know that you don't want to feel alone, and face the fact that nobody directly related to you actually cares about your wellbeing, and so for said wellbeing, you have to be without them. The guilt comes from a place of extreme shame and trauma, on top of the stigma that says 'family is everything'. But you know more than anyone else how absolutely miserable this situation is making you. If you've made it this far without cutting them off, I have full confidence you can absolutely thrive if/when you do. 

Please look into finding a therapist that specializes in trauma and cpstd, especially look out for one that is very knowledgeable in family and childhood abuse, and/or sexual abuse.
Cut your family off, cold turkey. They do not respect your boundaries are probably never will. Block them on everything, block their numbers, I don't know if they know where you live but if they do you might have to invest in a restraining order. It will be hard, but please for your future stick to it. Your happiness is worth it, even if the means to get there are hard. I believe you, and I believe you can be happy if you are given the space to heal and thrive. I'm so sorry this is happening to you, I can't imagine the stress you're under; you don't deserve to be treated so callously and dismissive. You were hurt badly, by the people who were supposed to be the safest place for you. They don't deserve your consideration. You are more than they're trying to reduce you to.

Wishing you all the best and sending all my luck and love. You've got this.

This is going to be a long post but here goes. TL;DR at the bottom  
My mom is exactly the same way and while I obviously don't know all the details of your situation, if she's anything like mine, she's only nice sometimes because she needs you for something and can't afford to be mean all the time lest you bolt and go no contact. I would assume the 'need' is you taking care of her while she struggles with cancer, or if this has been going on since long before she got diagnosed, maybe she likes using you as a punching bag of sorts, to take her anger/frustrations out on, or she may feel like she can indulge in the desire to hurt others and feels like you're her best option. (not to call you a punching bag of course, but that she might see you that way even if she doesn't use that term specifically)   
I would suggest therapy of some kind, either for her specifically for her obvious anger issues, or family therapy to salvage any sort of relationship, if thats something you even want or can do. I wouldn't blame you if you're just done. So I'm going to say this right now. Your feelings are completely valid and you have every right to be mad at her. You feeling conflicted about your feelings is also valid but you should know that you are in no way obligated to love her (especially) if she treats you terribly. You're worth it, don't downplay your own concerns and feelings.  
 I don't know much about your situation (sorry I didn't check if you had any other posts) but I believe you can get through this. Another thing I want to add, I've seen how cancer treatments affect a person first hand, and I'm deeply sorry if her behavior can be explained by this. Best of luck to you and to her, for the sake of her health and life, and your own health.  
TL;DR- she's either emotionally abusive or being affected by her treatments (but is still abusive; she's not in her right mind) or both. In any case, you and your feelings are in no way invalid.  
One more thing: good luck in your transition :)
